mil3.3.2:1.2: “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say ‘no first point is found’, give me a simile for that.”
mil3.3.2:1.3: “Suppose, Great King, a man were to put a small seed in the ground; from it a sprout would rise up, and in due course reach growth, increase, and abundance, and give fruit.
mil3.3.2:1.4: Taking a seed from that, he would plant it again; from that too a sprout would rise up, and in due course reach growth, increase, and abundance, and give fruit.
mil3.3.2:1.7: “In the same way, Great King, no first point of time is found.”
mil3.3.2:2.2: “Suppose, Great King, a hen had an egg, from the egg a hen, and from the hen an egg.
mil3.3.2:2.5: “In the same way, Great King, no first point of time is found.”
mil3.3.2:3.2: The elder drew a circle on the ground and said to King Milinda—
mil3.3.2:3.3: “Great King, does this circle have an end?”
mil3.3.2:3.5: “In the same way, Great King, these circles were spoken of by the Blessed One: ‘Dependent on the eye and visible forms, eye consciousness arises; the meeting of the three is contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, craving; with craving as condition, grasping; with grasping as condition, deeds; from deeds again an eye is born’.
mil3.3.2:4.2: and dependent on the mind and ideas, mind consciousness arises; the meeting of the three is contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, craving; with craving as condition, grasping; with grasping as condition, deeds; from deeds again a mind is born’.
mil3.3.2:4.5: “In the same way, Great King, no first point of time is found.”
